item.title: Wisconsin vs. Iowa series history ahead of 100th all-time meeting
item.description: Officially, this is set to be the 100th all-time meeting between the Wisconsin Badgers and Iowa Hawkeyes . There's nothing quite like rivalry week, and while the Battle for the Heartland Trophy hasn't gone the Badgers ' way in a few years, that should only add more fuel to the fire. Iowa dominated UW last season, 37-0. Badgers fans will remember that it came in a six-game stretch in which they scored a combined 41 points from Sept. 13 to Oct. 25. The Hawkeyes have been in possession of the trophy since 2022. Wisconsin hasn't beaten Iowa since Oct. 30, 2021, when they took care of business 27-7 in Madison. UW's last win in Iowa City was on Sept. 22, 2018, so it's been eight years since the Badgers have gone to Kinnick Stadium and taken care of business. Wisconsin barely leads the all-time series vs. Iowa All-time, Wisconsin is 49-48-2 against Iowa. The Badgers are just 20-27-1 on the road, so that's certainly something to monitor ahead of their Big Noon Kickoff on Halloween. This current four-game skid is tied for the second longest, but it's nowhere near as bad as when Iowa won 10 straight from 1985 to 1996. A 10-10 tie in 1984 helped lessen the blow as Iowa had also won seven in a row from 1977 to 1983. When was the first ever meeting? UW took care of business in the first-ever meeting between these two teams, 44-0, on Oct. 29, 1894. They wouldn't meet again until 1906, but it's worth noting that Wisconsin won its first six games against Iowa. item.title: ESPN’s Pat McAfee speaks out about ‘death threats’ targeting him and his family
item.description: ESPN personality Pat McAfee has spoken out about death threats directed at him and his family, revealing the personal toll of sustained online backlash. The former NFL punter shared a lengthy statement on X, describing his fears and the security concerns surrounding his work on College GameDay . McAfee said he had avoided his mentions and direct messages after receiving threatening messages earlier this month. However, he believes the threats remain widespread. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DM’s this month since these back to back days but.. I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee wrote. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” MORE: Utah, ESPN share statements amid Pat McAfee ‘College GameDay’ tension He also expressed concern about messages targeting his wife, daughter, and son. “It’s a weird time,” McAfee said. “The things that get said about what my daughter and son and wife deserve are all rather wild as well.” McAfee’s statement followed renewed criticism after the University of Utah shared a video mocking him on its official account. He also referenced a New York Times piece that he felt contributed to the negative attention surrounding him. Pat McAfee recalls heightened security at Tennessee Pat McAfee speaks during McAfee’s “Kicking is Easy” Contest at ESPN’s College GameDay at The Grove in Oxford, Miss. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) McAfee also detailed the security concerns surrounding last year’s College GameDay appearance in Tennessee. He said authorities feared a possible copycat incident following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. “The world, in front of the entire internet, just proved that we had gotten to a rather extreme place,” McAfee said. According to McAfee, the FBI, Disney security, Tennessee State Police, Knoxville police, and university police worked together to protect the event. He recalled that a bulletproof vest was even suggested as a precaution. “FBI snipers were sent down there, huge presence of police… it was a surreal moment,” McAfee explains. “The conversation about the death threats I had been receiving in life was definitely a huge topic. I don’t think it was the FBI that suggested the Bullet Proof Vest, but it was certainly an idea presented by one of the security groups. “We had no idea what to expect. Nobody had been in that type of situation before.” Despite the fear, he praised the security teams and students who supported him during the broadcast. He said he had never felt safer or more appreciative of the people around him that morning. McAfee believes the backlash intensified after his comments about Algerian Olympic gold medal-winning boxer Imane Khelif were presented without what he considered important context. He said subsequent mistakes and misquotes repeatedly fueled further hostility. MORE: Pat McAfee recounts terrible Utah College GameDay experience with tasteless Charlie Kirk refer

item.title: Sophie Cunningham reveals FBI is watching 20 stalkers as alleged stalker stays jailed
item.description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham says the FBI is monitoring roughly 20 people on her behalf. This revelation lands while her alleged stalker sits in jail. Cunningham, whose WNBA future is in flux ahead of free agency, told Theo Von on the This Past Weekend podcast about the downside of fame. “We do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do,” she said, then added that she has “20 people that the FBI are watching for me. Me alone.” MORE: Steve Kerr takes jab at WNBA Finals’ unusual Game 6 start time What did Cunningham tell Theo Von? Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) dribbles the ball against Las Vegas Aces. | Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images Cunningham said she wasn’t permitted to name the people under watch, but she identified one. “I know one of them, but yeah. I mean, he’s locked away now,” she said, later adding, “His name’s Kevin.” The former Missouri standout then joked about her miniature donkey of the same name, asking, “Do I need to rename Kevin?” Von joked that the donkey might be working for the stalker. Where does Kevin Singh’s case stand? Prosecutors charged Kevin Singh, 49, with stalking, intimidation and harassment after his June 23 arrest, and an affidavit states he hand-delivered a letter and a cologne-sprayed Guns N’ Roses T-shirt to Gainbridge Fieldhouse in September 2025. A detective wrote that Cunningham “feels like she is always watching her back, doesn’t feel safe and is fearful of Kevin Singh.” Singh remains in the Marion County Jail on a $40,000 bond after a judge rejected his bid for a reduction , and his trial is scheduled for early 2027. Cunningham is the second Fever player targeted in a stalking case, after a Texas man who harassed Fever star Caitlin Clark was sentenced in 2025 to 2 1/2 years in prison. Sophie Cunningham’s Fever free agency Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) warms up before playing the Toronto Tempo | Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Cunningham, 30, is an unrestricted free agent after playing 2026 on a one-year, $665,000 deal. She averaged 7.9 points across 43 games. The Fever finished a franchise-record 28-16 before falling to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round. “I don’t know what the offseason holds,” Cunningham said. “A lot of us are under free agency now, so who knows?” General manager Amber Cox said at exit interviews that “Sophie has had two really productive years for us, in terms of shooting the basketball.” She answered no when asked whether off-court attention would affect that evaluation. The Fever then parted ways with Cox and team president Kelly Krauskopf. Indiana’s new front office will decide whether to bring the veteran guard back. “Kelly and Amber, they’re phenomenal, phenomenal people ,” Cunningham said. item.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals plans to launch his own racing academy outside F1
item.description: Motorsport photo At just 20 years old, Andrea Kimi Antonelli is currently busy making the rest of the Formula 1 grid look like a bunch of sluggish retirees. But apparently, casually dominating the 2026 World Championship in a Mercedes isn't quite enough to keep the Italian phenom occupied. In a recent sit-down with Germany's Auto Motor und Sport , Antonelli revealed that he is already plotting his next massive move outside the F1 paddock: building his own driver academy. Following the recent paddock chatter around Lando Norris launching his own junior team , Antonelli wants a piece of the driver-development pie. And given that he literally grew up inside the garage of his father's GT racing team, AKM Motorsport, he knows exactly how brutal the financial ladder can be for a kid with talent but no cash. "We want to build an academy for young people so they get a chance in motorsport," Antonelli told AMUS. "Motorsport is a great but difficult world. It is not easy to get opportunities there. We want to help young drivers get a chance." The Verstappen GT3 FOMO Interestingly, Antonelli isn't focusing his future academy strictly on getting kids into the Formula 1 feeder series. He explicitly noted that professional GT racing is a highly viable, lucrative path - a mindset heavily fuelled by a certain three-time Dutch world champion. Max Verstappen has essentially turned the GT3 endurance world into his own personal side quest, and the rest of the F1 grid is collectively catching FOMO. Antonelli is no exception. "That doesn't necessarily have to be in Formula 1," he added. "There are also many opportunities in professional GT racing." item.title: Harry Kane makes ultimate gift promise to England and Bayern Munich teammates after emotional Ballon d'Or victory
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has revealed his plans to treat his Bayern Munich and England colleagues to special gifts following his historic Ballon d'Or triumph in London. The 33-year-old striker enjoyed an incredible 2026, scoring a combined 73 goals for club and country to claim football's most prestigious individual prize. Reaching the pinnacle Kane claimed his maiden Ballon d'Or on Monday night, edging out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to secure the prestigious accolade. The 33-year-old was honoured in his home city of London, where he delivered a gracious acceptance speech before celebrating at an exclusive Soho nightclub. The recognition follows a breathtaking 2026 campaign for the prolific frontman. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates finished the season with an 82-80 record. The highlight from this year’s team was the offense but the starting pitching was still solid this season. The question is should the Pirates add a veteran free agent arm for next season? The answer in my mind is yes, Pittsburgh absolutely needs to add experience and depth to that starting rotation. This is still a mostly young rotation with Paul Skenes, Jared Jones, Braxton Ashcraft and Bubba Chandler. Mitch Keller is one of the older starters on the club at 30 years old, so this is a very young group. Ashcraft was arguably the top pitcher for the Bucs with a 14-6 record and a 3.65 ERA. While Skenes finished with a 10-11 record 3.82 ERA. While both Keller and Jones missed serious time with injuries. The first veteran pitcher I think the Pirates should look at is Nick Martinez from the Tampa Bay Rays. Martinez helped lead the Rays to the World Series, where he had a 3.10 ERA over 31 starts while earning his first career All-Star nod in 2026. He doesn’t miss a ton of bats, but he averaged an MLB-low 1.30 walks per nine innings this year. The 36-year-old Martinez has a $20 million mutual option for 2027, but he seems likely to decline it and pursue a multi-year deal in free agency this offseason. Another Pitcher is Michael King from the San Diego Padres. King might be a little pricy, but I think he is worth it. The 31-year-old veteran is widely expected to opt out of the three-year, $75 million contract he signed with the Padres last December and re-enter free agency this winter. King struggled to stay healthy in 2025, but he bounced back to post a 3.21 ERA over 32 starts for San Diego this season. I understand some of these pitchers might be a little expensive, but this needs to be the offseason where the front office spends money. item.title: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace
item.description: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace Michael Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best players since Bayern Munich signed him from Crystal Palace for a reported €53 million in 2024. In an interview with FC Bayern’s club magazine, "51", board member for sport Max Eberl has revealed what convinced the German champions to sign the French winger. “He had a somewhat unsettled career path: he attended several elite football academies in England. But that kind of background doesn’t necessarily have to be a red flag – facing adversity can also help shape a player," Eberl said. “To get to know a footballer, above all, you have to talk to people who have experienced him as either a teammate or an opponent.” Conversations between Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund and his fellow Austrian Oliver Glasner, who was managing Crystal Palace at the time, proved particularly valuable in assessing Olise. “In Michael’s case, we had the advantage that Oliver Glasner was his manager at Crystal Palace at the time – and our sporting director, Christoph Freund, knows Glasner very well,” Eberl said. "When a manager says, ‘Of course, take him, take him,’ it makes you suspicious. But Glasner said, ‘He still has things to learn – and we could really use him.’ That told you he valued Michael highly. "And then there were the conversations with Michael himself: it’s a pleasure to talk football with him.”

item.title: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona
item.description: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona Real Madrid signed Bernardo Silva as a free agent back in the summer after his contract with Manchester City expired. Los Blancos secured his signature, beating the likes of Barcelona and Atletico Madrid to it, and expectations were high about what he could add to the midfield. However, it has taken some time for him to settle in, and Madrid’s victory over Barca at the Camp Nou seems like a turning point for the Portuguese midfielder. Bernardo Silva delivered his most convincing performance since arriving in the summer, justifying Jose Mourinho’s determination to bring him to the Bernabeu . According to Diario AS , Silva had long dreamed of representing Madrid, but his initial approach was rejected earlier this year. Mourinho’s return changed everything, with the manager personally pushing for his arrival despite interest from several other European clubs. Mourinho’s intervention changed Bernardo Silva’s future After deciding to leave Manchester City, Silva initially struggled to convince Madrid to pursue his signature. Bernardo Silva is slowly coming into his own at Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) His agent, Jorge Mendes, subsequently explored alternative destinations, with Barcelona emerging as a serious possibility. However, during a June meeting with Jose Angel Sanchez and Juni Calafat, Mourinho made his intentions clear. “We need a player like Bernardo Silva. We have to secure his signing,” the Portuguese manager insisted. Once Silva learned of Madrid’s interest, he paused other negotiations and prioritised the move. He eventually joined on a free transfer, signing a contract until 2028. Mourinho’s patience rewarded with impressive Clasico display Despite pushing for his signing, Mourinho deliberately managed Silva’s introduction into the team. He wanted the 32-year-old midfielder to regain his physical sharpness before assuming greater responsibilities. That patience paid off against Barcelona, where Silva helped Madrid dictate the tempo and maintain composure against a much more technical midfield. Will Bernardo be a started in the upcoming games? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His contribution was particularly important because Madrid had originally identified Rodri as their preferred option to provide control in midfield. While Silva is a different player from his former team-mate, he helped Madrid outplay a midfield featuring Rodri. The Clasico also showed why Silva’s experience matters for Madrid. There is no doubt that he will have an important role to play in the coming weeks . Silva has now taken an important step towards establishing himself as a regular starter, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the upcoming games.

item.title: 'She cold': Tyrese Maxey reacts to meeting Caitlin Clark for the first time ever
item.description: Credit: David Berding/Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images Tyrese Maxey starred for the Philadelphia 76ers in their win over the Indiana Pacers, but he experienced another major highlight off the court. The All-Star guard had the opportunity to meet WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark for the first time at the Gainbridge Fieldhouse, which is her home arena with the Indiana Fever. After the game, Maxey spoke about meeting Clark. Tyrese Maxey says he tried ‘not to fan out’ while meeting Caitlin Clark Clark is one of the biggest names in the WNBA. The 24-year-old has taken the women’s game to unprecedented heights, and she has earned a massive fan following as a result. Among her fans appears to be Maxey, who is a superstar himself, but he couldn’t hide his excitement when he met Clark during the 76ers’ win over the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night. Speaking after the game, he said on Wish TV News: “I think that’s the first time I’m really meeting her. Honestly, that’s just like, shoot, another person I like to watch. She cold. She nice. “So seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, you know? It was really cool seeing her. This is her building, she plays here. It was good seeing her. She’s nice.” Maxey’s candid admission that he had to stop himself from fanning out shows the enormous impact Clark has had in the world of basketball. The admiration there is absolutely fantastic to see, and we’re sure Maxey’s reaction to meeting the Indiana Fever star will not be forgotten by fans across the country. Up next for the Sixers is an NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks on Friday night. Maxey will be hoping to continue his good form in that game.

item.title: FDU basketball to wear jersey patch for special cause this season
item.description: Like a lot of men’s college basketball teams, FDU will debut a patch on its jerseys when the 2026-27 season gets underway next week. Unlike just about everyone else, that patch is not a corporate sponsorship designed to make money. Head coach Jack Castleberry had something else in mind. “What if we found a cause and championed that cause?” he said in pitching his idea to athletics director Jason Young. “It would be an opportunity for us to do some good here.” When the Knights’ take the court at third-ranked Illinois Monday, and for the remainder of their schedule, the upper right corner of their jerseys will read “NDSS” and in smaller letters, “National Down Syndrome Society.” The Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit's mission, “to create a world where individuals with Down syndrome thrive,” is close to Castleberry’s heart. His youngest daughter, 2-year-old Avery, has Down syndrome. And for Castleberry, his wife Kara and their two older daughters (ages 7 and 5), it’s been an eye-opening experience. “I think there’s a lot of misunderstanding out there about what Down syndrome actually is and what the lives are like for those who have Down syndrome,” said Castleberry, who lives in River Edge in Bergen County. “It’s not this terrible thing that I believe most people think it is.” When he and Kara found out Avery would be born with Down syndrome, “it shakes you a little bit” he said. But as he explained, borrowing a line from a book he read on the subject, that was the last bad day. “I can’t speak to everybody’s experience, but my kid is the happiest kid of the three I have,” he said. “She is such a joy. I never thought I would say something like this, but when you’re in front of her, no matter who you are, she sees you. She looks into your soul and there’s a genuine connection. That, I certainly didn’t expect. “You walk into the room with her and your day just brightens up.” Part of Castleberry’s motivation was that he noticed “stuff out there (on social media) about Down syndrome that wasn’t accurate, and to me that was sad,” he said, adding that some of it reached the point where “I felt a little bit threatened for my daughter.” Then he realized he’s got a pretty big forum – FDU’s opener at Illinois will be nationally televised by the Big Ten Network – and the ability to do something about that. “I genuinely proud, and I’m thankful that our administration is not only willing to consider something like this, but adamant about us doing it,” Castleberry said. For the National Down Syndrome Society, this partnership is the first of its kind. “It was really nice to be able to connect with Jack, and that means so much to us because families are at the core of what we do,” said Michelle Sagan, the nonprofit’s director of communications and marketing, who has a sister with Down syndrome. “We hope people see the patch, hear about Down syndrome on the broadcasts, and it really helps people understand our population.” The partnership will extend beyond a patch.

As with Bosa, the team has to be cautious with Evans to ensure he’s ready for the playoff push. Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., Cleveland’s Jerry Jeudy and the Colts’ Josh Downs (who requested a trade Wednesday) are among the wideouts who could be available for something less than a premium draft pick. If the Niners truly want to swing for the fences, they could try to pry loose a superstar. Raiders end Maxx Crosby and Jets wideout Garrett Wilson are names that move the needle, but they’re unlikely trade candidates barring a significant offer — one with multiple top picks, probably including multiple first-rounders.” 49ers release struggling cornerba ck “Atlanta picked on Jones in coverage. He allowed four of his five targets to be completed for 49 yards, allowing a passer rating of 107.5. In five games this season, Jones was targeted over 30% of the time when he was on the field. Add in the penalties, and he became unplayable, since the run defense and tackling were a struggle. The 49ers will actually save money by releasing Jones, according to Over the Cap. He signed a one-year deal, and the contract has no guaranteed money beyond what appears to be a $140,000 signing bonus. Cornerback Nate Hobbs remains on the injured reserve. item.title: Travis Kelce explains exactly why Seattle Seahawks are so hard to play against right now
item.description: Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Travis Kelce breaks down what Mike MacDonald has done with the Seattle Seahawks which makes them so difficult to beat. The Kansas City Chiefs were handed their first loss of the season in pretty spectacular fashion by the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The reigning Super Bowl champions won 20-3, completely shutting off Kenneth Walker III and Patrick Mahomes. It was no mean feat, as both have been in fine form to start the year. Travis Kelce has been looking like his old self for the most part, too. He wasn’t able to do much either, though. Kelce had four receptions in the game for 44 yards. He spoke about what makes the Seattle defence special. Travis Kelce breaks down Mike MacDonald’s defensive preference which makes Seattle tough The Seattle Seahawks have been the NFL’s best defence by total yards allowed this season, giving up just 233.9 yards per game. That’s No. 1 in the league. They’ve been excellent at limiting their opponents, with a sizeable gap between them and the second-ranked Minnesota Vikings. Kelce, in conversation with his brother Jason on their podcast, addressed how head coach Mike MacDonald is able to make that happen. “I feel like every time I face McDonald, he stays true to his style, and he has the personnel to be able to execute how he wants to,” the tight end said. “He’s going to kind of want to keep everything in front of him in terms of the back end of things. “But he’s always got an unbelievable D-line that just makes it tough to get to the second level on your double teams. It really forces you to be great on the backside of runs where, it’s typically the ball ends up coming back to that gap.” MacDonald became the first head coach in NFL history to win the Super Bowl while still being the primary defensive play-caller. The Seahawks are just 4-3 this season, but with their defense, one can never really write them off. item.title: Marc Marquez wary of MotoGP title rival Jorge Martin at Sepang: "Adrenaline is the best painkiller"
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP points leader Marc Marquez claims to be wary of Jorge Martin's potential if his rival is passed fit to race at Sepang this weekend. Martin fractured his wrist in a heavy crash during the sprint race in Australia last weekend, falling 10 points behind Marquez in the championship. Factory Aprilia rider Martin has been declared fit to take part in Friday's opening session in Malaysia, but most expect him to be compromised if he races at all. Read Also: Jorge Martin braced for “really difficult, painful” MotoGP weekend with broken arm His Ducati counterpart Marquez said he wasn't buying that line. He referenced the stricter medical clearance threshold introduced since Marquez seriously compounded injuries by returning too soon after a crash at Jerez in 2020. "I feel and I believe that with the new protocols we have after my injury at Jerez, if they declare him fit, it means that he's able to ride," said the 33-year-old. "And if he's able to ride, he will be at a very high level because adrenaline is the best painkiller." Speaking in his native Spanish, Marquez went a step further in talking up his opponent: "I’m not just confident he’ll be fast on track, I'm certain of it. It won’t change how I approach my own work, but I’ll certainly be pushing to the maximum." Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team The Spaniard also welcomed his countryman's efforts to race in Malaysia, saying it was better for the show. "Yeah, of course for the championship fight it's better that Jorge is there. I'm happy to see Martin on track." While Marquez offers soundbites designed not to tempt fate, it is worth pointing out that he landed what appeared to be a major psychological blow on Martin at Phillip Island. The 2024 world champion fell off during a close battle with Marquez , despite being the faster rider. That mental setback came on top of a not dissimilar mistake at the previous sprint in Indonesia, in which he was also quicker than Marquez. On that occasion, Martin was forced to give Marquez the lead due to tyre pressure concerns, but erred as he attempted to hit the front again. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: How Kimi Antonelli can win 2026 F1 title in Mexico City without even finishing race
item.description: Kimi Antonelli is on the cusp of becoming Formula 1 ’s youngest-ever world champion and looks set to claim the 2026 drivers’ title at the Mexican Grand Prix . The 20-year-old has made a mockery of the pre-season predictions which put his Mercedes teammate George Russell as the title favourite, with nine grand prix victories and 15 podiums in total. After his win in Austin, Antonelli currently has a 123-point lead over Russell with five rounds (and no sprint races) remaining this season, assuming F1 fulfils its end-of-season schedule with Qatar and Abu Dhabi. If those races can’t take place due to the conflict in the Middle East, a one-off round would conclude the campaign in Imola. item.title: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United
item.description: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United After 11 Premiership games, and having played every other team once, Celtic find themselves four points clear at the top of the table. Martin O’Neill’s side are four points better off than at this stage last season and have won nine out of their 11 games in the campaign. Indeed, the only points dropped have been in two home games, and while Thursday night’s 2-2 draw with Dundee United saw the Champions maintain their Premiership lead, there was also a sense of frustration that it couldn’t have been extended. However, reflecting on the game, Martin O’Neill said that in a game his side should have won, over the course of the campaign it could still prove to be a valuable point gained, given the team had to come from behind. “It was a tough old game for us,” the Celtic manager told CelticPlayer . “I thought the second half performance was very strong and we had attack after attack. Yet, remarkably, they could have scored on a breakaway. “It was a big, big second half for us and we deserved the equaliser at least. And I just thought we were going to come up trumps towards the end. “The boys have given a lot in the game and they'll have to do the same again in a few days’ time. “We're going to be playing against Falkirk who are up for the game themselves. So it's just resting up, doing a little bit of work, but not that much because the games have been coming thick and fast.” CELTICPLAYER UNIQUE ANGLE Celtic drew 2-2 with Dundee United on Wednesday night to remain four points clear at the top of the table. item.title: ‘Drawing a blank’ – Robert Saleh seemingly forgets motivational speech for Titans in awkward clip
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Robert Saleh was speaking to reporters and describing what he said to the Tennessee Titans before he completely lost his train of thought. Saleh has been under the microscope ever since he took over as head coach of the Titans, following a second stint as the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers. The Titans have started the season 1-6 and have not looked great under Saleh. And his latest awkward moment during a press conference has only raised more questions about his fit as head coach. Robert Saleh loses his train of thought over Titans motivational talk during press conference Speaking to reporters ahead of the Tennessee Titans’ loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, HC Robert Saleh spoke about what he told the players as they continue to find their stride. While explaining his mindset to the reporters, Saleh began describing his message to the team, before immediately losing his train of thought. Saleh said: “We’ve just got to keep going through the process of learning how to finish. In the most extreme times, and this is what I told the team about today, and this is for all humans, not just football players. “In the most adverse moments, in the most pressure-packed moments, you’re always going to be… ummm… I’m drawing a blank. (to assistant coach) Do you remember what I said?” It was an awkward look for Saleh, who is already under pressure for not getting the most out of a young Titans team that many felt had a lot of potential coming into the new season. It doesn’t help that Saleh’s previous stint as head coach of the New York Jets ended disastrously, as management let him go for failing to get the best out of Aaron Rodgers and a strong offensive unit early into the 2024 season. item.title: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter
item.description: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter Manchester United travel to West London to take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime. The Red Devils have faced off against the Blues 199 times , meaning this match will be the 200th competitive game between the two rivals. United have come out on top 85 times in history, with Chelsea winning 57. There have also been 57 draws during the storied fixture. Here are three storylines to get the blood pumping. United closing in on unwanted record After Michael Carrick’s side lost 0-3 at home to AFC Bournemouth last Sunday, they had officially gone six Premier League matches without a win. This is already the second-longest winless streak in their Premier League history. The longest arrived in May 2025 when they went eight matches without a win. Nonetheless, with matches against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool to come, it is not exactly clear where the next win will come from. United are still some way off their worst ever run, not winning in 16 consecutive matches way back in the 1929-1930 season. Chelsea record Fortunately, the Red Devils have quite a respectable record as of late against Saturday’s opponents. In their last ten matches against the Blues, they have only lost twice. There have been four United wins, including two last season, and four draws since 2021. Former players Man United and Chelsea have had a lot of former players play for one another over the years. Andrey Santos has not had the best start to his United career, but he moved from Chelsea in the summer and, with Kobbie Mainoo still out, he will likely get another chance to start in the midfield against his former team. One player United will not want to face is their former player Danny Welbeck. The Carrington youth product moved to Stamford Bridge in the summer and has haunted United many times in the past, scoring six times against them for Brighton and Arsenal.

item.title: Iraola praises Liverpool teenager after man-of-the-match Chelsea performance
item.description: Iraola praises Liverpool teenager after man-of-the-match Chelsea performance Andoni Iraola praised the performance of Trey Nyoni after the Liverpool midfielder was named man of the match during the club’s Carabao Cup win over Chelsea. Liverpool reached the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after beating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties at Anfield, following a 1-1 draw in normal time. Iraola opted to rotate his team for the clash, ahead of a Premier League meeting with Arsenal this weekend, and handed Nyoni a start in central midfield. The 19-year-old has been on the fringes of the first team this season and impressed, earning the Player of the Match award from Liverpool’s official social media channels. Iraola said Nyoni did ‘very well’ and was pleased how his youngsters handled the occasion, with academy graduate Lewis Koumas also starting against Chelsea. “I think he has done very well. Really well. It’s good for the young players especially to live these experiences in cup competitions, where if you lose you are out,” Iraola said in his post-match press conference. “We have been losing and then the draw. Then they haven’t been there in the penalty shootout but they lived the feelings. They played under pressure against a very good team. item.title: South Korea boss backs Son as captain after rift rumours
item.description: Son Heung-min has been called up by South Korea for friendlies next month against Saudi Arabia and Qatar (Philip FONG) Son Heung-min will continue as South Korea captain despite reports of friction between the former Tottenham striker and his senior international team-mates, coach Robert Moreno said Thursday. Moreno named Son, now 34 and playing for LAFC in Major League Soccer, in his squad for friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Qatar next month. He also selected experienced Europe-based trio Kim Min-jae, Hwang Hee-chan and Hwang In-beom, who reports say were ready to quit the national team last month. Moreno said he had held "many conversations with the players" since taking over on an interim basis after South Korea's World Cup flop in North America. "I spent more time communicating than training," the Spaniard said at a press conference that lasted more than an hour. "Even in the best teams people can have different opinions. What matters is how those differences are resolved." Moreno's contract is set to expire after the two friendlies, although South Korean football chiefs could keep him on for the Asian Cup, scheduled for Saudi Arabia in January. When asked about Son's leadership role in the team, Moreno said: "The captain is Son Heung-min. I have nothing more to say." Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of a 0-0 home friendly draw with Venezuela this month. Kim said afterwards that "every player needs to put their head down and give it their all", fuelling talk of divisions within the squad. Moreno said "the team is healthy" and backed the players to work together. "I believe you can find the answer in what I have said today and the squad that has been announced," he said. South Korea's football association this month told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks" on players. The national team is in the crosshairs after a poor showing at the World Cup, which saw coach Hong Myung-bo quit after they failed to get past the group stage. amk/pst

item.title: Bearman Has Scored 23 of Haas’s 30 Points. Now He Reportedly Wants $6.7 Million
item.description: Oliver Bearman has scored 23 of Haas’s 30 points in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and he reportedly wants to be paid like it: €6 million, about $6.7 million, a year to stay with the team. The figure comes from F1 business writer Marc Limacher, as Read Motorsport reported . Haas is reportedly unwilling to pay it, which has slowed talks on a 2027 deal, as we reported this week . Neither Bearman nor Haas has confirmed the number. What Bearman Is Paid Now RacingNews365’s estimates of 2026 base salaries put Bearman on about $1 million, among the lowest on the grid. Teams don’t publish contracts, and the estimates leave out bonuses and personal sponsorship, according to RacingNews365 . Here’s how that compares with points scored after 18 rounds: Driver Team Estimated 2026 salary 2026 points Max Verstappen Red Bull $70 million 236 Lewis Hamilton Ferrari $60 million 241 Esteban Ocon Haas $7 million 7 Isack Hadjar Red Bull $5 million 105 Kimi Antonelli Mercedes $2 million 365 Oliver Bearman Haas $1 million 23 Liam Lawson Racing Bulls $1 million 77 The raise Bearman is reportedly asking for would put him at about what his teammate is estimated to earn. Ocon, who leaves Haas after this season, has 7 points. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has won nine Grands Prix on an estimated $2 million. Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid on Sept. 12, 2026. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) Why Bearman Says It’s Out of His Hands Haas has already confirmed Ferrari junior Rafael Cámara as Ocon’s replacement for 2027, but it hasn’t confirmed Bearman alongside him. Both sides say they want to keep going. “I think on our side as well, if I’m not mistaken, we’re very sure that we want to continue working together, and the only sticking points are kind of out of my hands, more contractual points,” Bearman told reporters at the US Grand Prix. He’s also a Ferrari junior, and he made it clear Haas isn’t where he plans to end up. “In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with, and I see my future with,” he said. “But at some point, as well, I feel like I’ve earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top four team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal.” For now, Ferrari has Charles Leclerc on a long-term deal and Lewis Hamilton in the other seat. Haas is seventh in the constructors’ standings with 30 points, and Bearman’s 23 points put him 13th in the drivers’ championship. The next race is the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, Nov. 1, the next chance for either side to say where the talks stand.

item.title: Chelsea injury nightmare deepens as Xabi Alonso provides update on Maxence Lacroix blow against Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Chelsea’s injury problems have gone from bad to worse after Maxence Lacroix was forced to withdraw during their Carabao Cup showdown against Liverpool. The French defender appeared to suffer a hamstring issue during the first half at Anfield, adding further strain to Xabi Alonso’s already depleted squad. Lacroix limps off at Anfield The Blues crashed out of the Carabao Cup following a tense penalty shootout, with normal time ending 1-1 after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo traded spot-kicks. However, the loss of their commanding centre-back will be of far greater concern to the Chelsea coaching staff. Lacroix pulled up while chasing Gakpo through midfield shortly after Liverpool's equaliser. He went down off the ball moments later and required treatment on the pitch before being replaced by Levi Colwill. The Frenchman walked slowly to the dressing room in clear distress, clutching the back of his left thigh while consulting with the club's medical trainers. Alonso reacts to fresh fitness setback Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted the club will have to wait before discovering the full extent of the defender's muscle issue. Speaking after the final whistle, the Spaniard confirmed the medical team's initial suspicions. "Too early to tell. Probably he felt something on the hamstrings," Alonso said. "And we need a couple of days to check what's going to be the injury.” Mounting problems at Stamford Bridge Losing Lacroix represents a massive blow to Chelsea's defensive stability. The summer signing from Crystal Palace has been an ever-present figure this season, starting all eight Premier League fixtures and featuring in both Carabao Cup matches. His absence exacerbates an already severe selection crisis for Alonso. The west London outfit travelled north without Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, and Reece James due to injury, while talisman Cole Palmer missed the tie through suspension. Waiting game for the Blues Chelsea's medical staff will assess Lacroix over the coming days to determine a precise recovery timeline. A prolonged absence would stretch the squad to its limits, leaving Alonso heavily reliant on Colwill and his remaining defensive options during a busy autumn schedule. The manager must now regroup his depleted squad as they look to shake off their cup elimination and maintain momentum in the Premier League.

The Frenchman walked slowly to the dressing room in clear distress, clutching the back of his left thigh while consulting with the club's medical trainers. Alonso reacts to fresh fitness setback Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted the club will have to wait before discovering the full extent of the defender's muscle issue. Speaking after the final whistle, the Spaniard confirmed the medical team's initial suspicions. "Too early to tell. Probably he felt something on the hamstrings," Alonso said. "And we need a couple of days to check what's going to be the injury.” Mounting problems at Stamford Bridge Losing Lacroix represents a massive blow to Chelsea's defensive stability. The summer signing from Crystal Palace has been an ever-present figure this season, starting all eight Premier League fixtures and featuring in both Carabao Cup matches. His absence exacerbates an already severe selection crisis for Alonso. The west London outfit travelled north without Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, and Reece James due to injury, while talisman Cole Palmer missed the tie through suspension. Waiting game for the Blues Chelsea's medical staff will assess Lacroix over the coming days to determine a precise recovery timeline. A prolonged absence would stretch the squad to its limits, leaving Alonso heavily reliant on Colwill and his remaining defensive options during a busy autumn schedule. The manager must now regroup his depleted squad as they look to shake off their cup elimination and maintain momentum in the Premier League.

item.title: Time and owners not on Moyes’ side as he tries to end Everton trophy drought
item.description: The Friedkin Group want to sell and squad investment has dried up but Carabao Cup is still an opportunity for silverware A European challenge plus a concerted effort to end a trophy drought that will soon stretch into a 32nd year were Everton’s stated aims for this season, although that was before the club’s owners turned the taps off in the transfer market and announced they were looking to sell up. An abrupt change of direction and ambition from The Friedkin Group (TFG) has not altered the demands on David Moyes, however. It is as you were for the Everton manager, regardless of the tools at his disposal. Newcastle’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Thursday – when they will be backed by 7,732 fans after Everton allocated their opponents 15% of the ground – is timely on several counts. It is, first and foremost, an opportunity for Moyes’s team to advance in a competition that Everton have never won and edge closer to realising one stated aim for the campaign. It is also a chance to restore positivity after consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal , Everton’s only losses of the season. Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
